# Programs both backends build and run

The programs of one file the C and the LLVM backends' tests share, each a feature at a time. Every program here goes through `snello build` and runs as a native binary; the file beside it, `name.out`, is exactly what it prints. `go test ./compiler/emit/llvm/ ./compiler/emit/c/` builds every program here through both backends, as a release and a debug build, and compares its output with the `.out` file; a program without one fails the test. As each slice of a backend lands, the programs it makes buildable are added here.

The programs a reader starts from are under `examples/`; the book's chapters point here for the program each is cut from. To build one:

```
go build -o snello ./cmd/snello
./snello build compiler/emit/internal/backendtest/testdata/fib.snello
./fib
```

The binary is written to the current directory, named after the file.

| File | What it exercises |
|---|---|
| fib.snello | Recursion, integer and float arithmetic, sized integers, conversions |
| strings.snello | `Lines` over text with a carriage return, an empty line, an empty string and a trailing newline; the character classes of a byte; `min` and `max` over integers, floats and a literal; A `ref string` parameter, concatenation, comparison, byte indexing, `Sprintf`, `Printf`, `Sprint` |
| lent.snello | Borrows a call returns, of a string, a slice, a map, a struct, a value with a `Drop`, an option and a `Result`, in every place the compiler could take one for a value made there and release it: on either side of a `+` and in a chain of them, through `??`, an `if` and a `match`, as a statement of its own, passed, compared, converted, ranged over, sliced and printed; after each form the lender holds what it was made with, and a debug build reports a block released early or left at the end |
| optional-borrows.snello | An option of a `ref` borrow, which the LLVM backend writes as the pointer with null for `None`, beside one of a `ref string` and a `ref []int`, which stays a pair: made with `Some` and `None`, read with `??`, `?`, `Expect`, an if-binding and a `match`, asked `IsSome` and `IsNone`, mapped, stored in a struct, a tuple and a `Result`, nested, passed and returned, through a generic function, of a struct, an enum and a borrow, and taken from the library, a deque's `Get`, `Front` and iterator, a map's `Get` and a slice's `First` |
| returned-borrows.snello | A borrow of a parameter returned inside a tuple, a struct, an option of a tuple and a tuple within a tuple; a tuple of a local's borrow used within its function; an owned clone in a tuple; a closure that copies an `int` returned inside a tuple. The borrows of locals the same literals would carry out are refused, `compiler/types/testdata/errors/literal-borrow-escapes.snello` |
| tuple-types.snello | A tuple literal returned as a type declared over a tuple, plain and generic, and the value taken apart as the tuple the type stands for; a tuple literal's element converted to its slot as a struct field's value is, a `chan int` to a `<-chan int` and a struct to a trait it implements |
| named-views.snello | Methods of types declared over a string and a slice, whose `ref` receiver is the view itself, called by the compiler's helpers as a direct call calls them: `String` and `Error` when `fmt` prints the value, `Eq` and `Hash` when it keys a map, `Cmp` when a slice of it is sorted, `Clone`, and `String` through a trait value's table |
| lent-values.snello | Values lent where a borrow is wanted, followed through the steps that make them: a variant's `ref` field and `Some` given an owned variable lend it, which stays the variable's, used after and dropped once; a string chosen among literals lent through a call and kept past its statement; an element of a tuple made here returned with what it lends beside one borrowing a value made here; a value read through a borrow of a local returned by value; a borrow read out of a local through a borrow of it, a field, an element, a part matched through a borrow, an element ranged over through one, or a tuple taken apart through one, returned, kept in a variable first or read through two borrows; a `ref` written of a borrow variable or a field holding one, passed on; a `ref ref` parameter's result; a borrow of a borrow variable's slot; a struct of borrows rebuilt from its own fields. The borrows the same steps would carry past their owners are refused, `compiler/types/testdata/errors/lent-through-values.snello` |
| assignment-base-call.snello | An assignment whose place is reached through a call: the value is made first and the call runs at the store, once, so a value that grows the slice the call reaches into is stored where the call then points, and a string stored through a pointer a call gives drops the old one there, on both backends |
| pointer-keys.snello | A map keyed by owned pointers, which compare and hash by what they point at: a second pointer to an equal value finds the entry, on both backends |
| blank.snello | The blank name in a function's `var` declarations holds nothing, its value dropped once every value of the declaration is made, as `:=` drops its blank's: a number, typed and inferred, a call's value, a string moved in, one of a pair and of a tuple, a value with a `Drop`, values that borrow, a `ref` and a `mut` changed after the declaration, a closure's capture moved after it and a borrow of a temporary, and the order of the drops against `:=` |
| control.snello | `if`/`else if`, the three forms of `for`, `continue` and `break`, a loop whose condition and step call functions, a named number type, swap by parallel assignment, `defer` |
| corners.snello | What the lowering to C must get right: literal bases, wrapping overflow, trigraph-looking strings, float printing |
| leave-early.snello | A value made before an operand whose `?` leaves the function, dropped once when it leaves and taken whole when it does not: an argument, a receiver, a struct, tuple, slice and map literal's element, a variadic argument |
| variadic.snello | Variadic functions: `...T` of numbers and of values with a `Drop`, moved in and dropped by the function; `...ref T` with a temporary dropped after the call and owned values lent without `ref`; a slice passed on, moved or lent, and passed on again; no arguments; a method, a trait's method through a trait value, with and without arguments, and through a bound; generic functions of each form, a function value and a closure; a deferred and a spawned call; a lent call in a loop; arguments evaluated left to right |
| constants.snello | Constants the checker folds: declared after their use, shifts, an unsigned mask, a negative division, remainder and shift, floats rounded to `f64` and `f32` and a negative zero, a declared number type, conversions from another package's constant, a string used as a format, a struct constant of expressions, a local constant, array lengths that are constants, an array used only by `len`; each beside the same arithmetic at run time |
| defaults.snello | Default field values: a constant of each kind a field has, a struct one among them; keyed literals that leave fields out and positional ones that stop before the last; literals in package variables and an array of them; a generic struct's default; a struct with a `Drop` and a string default; values passed and returned; the library's `os.OpenOptions` |
| conversions.snello | Conversions between a declared type and its underlying type, each a value that owns memory moved under the other name and freed once: a string, a slice, a map, an option, an array, a struct both ways, a slice of values with a `Drop`; from a variable, a field, a call's result and in a loop, as an argument and returned; and a struct without a zero value only for its defaults |
| drop-fields.snello | A value whose type implements `Drop` gives up a field only by leaving another in its place: `replace` and `take`, a clone, a borrow of a variant's part, each `Drop` seeing a field that holds a value; and `replace` and `take` of an owned pointer in a field, through a borrow of its struct, lent itself and optional, each at the place of the pointer |
| const-before-type.snello | Struct constants declared before their struct's type, one inside another, and given to an attribute: the type defined once, where the first of them needs it |
| attrs-program.snello | A program's own attributes beside a library's: help text, bounds and a secret read by two reflecting functions of the program, `json.Name` and `json.Skip` by `encoding/json`; a field read as the type its match on `f.type` took, and a value an arm binds that the arm a field takes does not read |
| attrs.snello | Attributes read at compile time: on a field, a variant and a type, a conversion over a string, a struct of constants, a struct with no fields written by its name and a constant's name; an instance of a generic type reading its declaration's; `None` where none is written |
| trait-arms.snello | Arms of a match on a type that name a trait: a type that implements it takes the arm, its method called on a value and its function on the type, before a kind's arm; a type that does not takes the next. Inside a trait arm, a kind's arm reaches the type's parts: a struct's fields read, built and their attributes looked up, an enum's variants named, two trait arms deep as well as one, and a trait arm inside a kind's, which keeps the kind |
| type-funcs.snello | Functions of a type: one calling another of its type, one with type parameters of its own, one of a generic type's instance, one a trait requires called through a bound on a type parameter, ones taken as values, deferred and spawned ones, a value boxed into a trait that requires one, one a trait's default body calls on Self, and one of a generic type that matches on the type's parameter and walks its fields |
| for-conditions.snello | A for loop's condition is evaluated on every pass, whatever writing it takes: a map read by a key computed or held in a variable the body changes, in a three-part loop and a loop on a condition alone, and the length of a slice of a slice or of a string from an index the body moves |
| for-post-moves.snello | A for loop's post statement that moves or replaces an owned value runs on every pass: a string moved in from a variable the body makes again, a struct's field given a new string, an option of a string emptied, and an int counted as before. So does one whose place is found by a call, an element at an index a function gives and a field of what a function lends, and a map's slot while the body grows the map |
| move-order-nested.snello | Operands evaluated left to right when a later one moves, somewhere inside it, a value an earlier one reads: a struct, an option, a slice, a tuple and a map literal around the moved value, a nested struct, a channel send and a returned tuple; a map literal's key moved or made by a call, after an earlier operand reads or calls; and a closure, called by an earlier operand, reading a value a later one moves |
| move-order.snello | Operands evaluated left to right when a later one moves a value an earlier one reads: a tuple, a call's and a method's arguments, a struct, a slice, a map and a variant literal, and a nested call |
| reflect.snello | Reflection at compile time: a match on a type parameter taking the arm of a type, a type declared over it taking the wildcard and not its underlying type's arm, a declared type's own arm with its method, of an option, slice, map, owned pointer or generic type, with a nested match on a shape's name; a loop over a struct's fields reading each; a value built from its fields, a `?` leaving after owned fields are made; an enum's variants, one arm each, read and built back by name, a recursive enum among them; a field's default and an option's `None` for a missing field; a trait's default body matching on the trait's type parameter and passing `Self` to a generic function that matches on it |

| iterators.snello | Generic traits: an `Iterator<T>` trait with a required `Next` and default adapters, one with a type parameter of its own, a `Range` implementing `Iterator<int>`, generic `MapIter` and `FilterIter` structs bounded by the trait and implementing it over their own parameters, a chain of `Map`, `Filter` and `Collect` over a named function and over closures, a generic method called on a call's result, and a `mut` method called on a temporary |
| arrays.snello | Arrays in the backend: an array of strings written to, printed, cloned inside a struct and dropped with every element released; an array of arrays; an array literal with the rest zero; an array copied whole and changed apart; a struct holding an array compared through its own `Eq`; a range over an array by value, `ref` and `mut`, of a variable, a package variable, a field and a call's result, an owned one consumed with each element dropped once, after a `break` too |

| group.snello | A group of tasks: members added by their handles and waited for together, `Wait` Ok once every member returned and the first panic among them when one failed, `Done` ended for a member that stops when told, a group of a thousand members and one of none, and what a failed member owned dropped before `Wait` returns |
| select.snello | `select` over receives and sends, with and without `default`: a case chosen at random among two ready channels, a send ready only while a receiver waits, a bare receive dropping its value, and an ended channel's `None` |

| unicode.snello | Text beyond ASCII: `ToUpper` and `ToLower` by Unicode's full case mapping, `ß` to `SS` and `İ` to `i` with a combining dot, a byte that is not UTF-8 read as U+FFFD, `Fields` and `Trim` on Unicode white space, `Split` with an empty separator by UTF-8 sequence and on an empty string, `Repeat`, `Join` and a `Builder`, `Contains` on a long text, and `Sort` on a struct through its `Cmp`|
| clocks.snello | Time arithmetic as Go's: a `Time` in 2286 round-tripping through `Unix`, comparisons across centuries, `Sub` saturating at the longest `Duration` either way, `Unix` rounding down and carrying nanoseconds into seconds, two `Now`s compared and subtracted on the monotonic clock, an `After` handing over a whole `Time` the runtime's timer made, `Duration.String` over every branch of Go's algorithm with `Round`, `Truncate` and `Abs` from Go's tests, a `Time` printed in UTC as Go prints one, across leap days, the first year and the year 9999, and a `Ticker` stopped or reset after a tick no one received, which leaves nothing in its channel |
| formats.snello | Printing as Go prints: floats in the shortest form with Go's exponent rule, `+Inf`, `-Inf` and `NaN`, an `f32` at its own precision, a precision on `%v`, `%s`, `%q` and `%d`, `%q` escaped as `strconv.Quote` escapes and an integer quoted as its rune, a `fmt.Stringer` printed as its `String` alone and inside a struct, `math.Abs`, `Min` and `Max` and the predeclared `min` and `max` on `-0` and `NaN`, `ParseFloat`'s grammar and the `Kind` of its error, and an `Rc`, a `Weak` and an `Arena` printed as what they hold |
| runes.snello | Text whole, the program chapter 19 is cut from: a range over a string giving each rune and its byte offset, `s.Runes()` and `string(rs)`, the counted loop over bytes, a string that is not valid UTF-8, the `unicode` package's classes, derived properties, categories, scripts and values, full case mapping and title case by words, `EqualIgnoreCase`, `unicode/utf8`, `unicode/utf16` as units and bytes, the normalization forms, and graphemes, words and sentences |
| zero.snello | No empty values, the program chapter 18 is cut from: the zero values of the types that have one, an optional where a value may be missing, a value built where it is declared when it depends on a condition, an optional `rc.Weak`, `replace` on a field of a type with no zero value and on an optional pointer, a map of such values read with `Get`, `strings.Repeat`'s option and a `WaitGroup` that will not count below zero |

| failures.snello | `bufio` when the file under it fails part way: a `Writer` keeping its first error for every later call and never writing a byte twice, a `Reader` keeping what it had read before a failure for the next `ReadString`, a `Scanner` giving the partial last line before `Err` |
| streams.snello | The edges of `io`, `bufio` and `os`: an `io.NewError` and the three ways an `Error` prints, with a path, without one, and with no `Op`; `ReadToString` naming the step that failed, on a directory and on an empty path; `WriteString` and `Remove` of a file, of a missing one and of a full directory; `MkdirTemp` putting its number where the pattern's last `*` is, and refusing a pattern with a `/`; `io.Copy` refusing a writer that claims more than it was given; a `Scanner` refusing a line past the limit `Buffer` set, over a reader that gives a few bytes a call and over a file; a `Reader` asked again after the end of the input, as a file being appended to is; and a `Writer` keeping its first error for an empty write too, with a size of zero taken as the default |
| alloc.snello | The allocator across tasks: strings of every size class and larger made by four tasks at once and released by `main` on another thread, each checked byte by byte on arrival and every tenth kept and checked again at the end, so a block handed out twice would show |

| assignment-order.snello | An assignment evaluates, left to right, the index and key operands of the places it writes, then the values it writes, and only then stores: a key a call gives before the value another gives, an index read before a value that changes it, an entry a store makes counted by no value, and several places and values in one assignment |
| value-before-store.snello | A value made before it is stored, borrows too: a borrow given itself, through a call, a `match` or an `if`, two borrows swapped, a field, an option and a tuple given what they hold, and a name shadowing the borrow it is declared from, each keeping what it read; an owned string, slice, struct, value with a `Drop` and `int` given to its own place, kept whole and dropped once |
| iterate.snello | A range over any value with `Next`: one variable or a pair, an iterator lent or consumed, a map type with `Next` ranged as an iterator, a map's `Entry` from any place, below 0 and past the end |
| borrow-index.snello | An element reached by an index that calls, or of a call's result, matched, bound, lent and taken in place, the index computed once |
| constant-borrows.snello | A borrow of a constant outlives the function that took it, so a function may return one: a literal of each kind, `true`, a struct constant, a constant of this package and of another, each read after the stack the function ran on has been written over |
| defer-prints.snello | A deferred print holds what it prints until the function returns: a whole temporary it owns, a value worked out of a temporary's part when the defer statement runs, and a part of a variable that lives as long; a format, a literal or a constant, held as it is |
| deque.snello | The deque's buffer of untagged slots: elements that own memory pushed at both ends, wrapped, grown, changed in place, cleared and dropped with the deque, every block counted in a debug build |
| empty-array.snello | A zero-length array: its literal, its zero value and a field of one in a generic struct with a `Drop` |
| guarded-reads.snello | A read that writes statements of its own runs only where it is evaluated: behind `&&` and `||` when the left side decides, and in its turn among a call's arguments; a map read saving its key, a slice of a slice, an element or a field of a value built in place |
| if-value-conditions.snello | An `if` used as a value drops its condition's temporaries once the condition is decided, before either branch runs, as an `if` statement does: an `else if` lending a constant, building a string or taking a lock that its branch takes again |
| operand-order.snello | Operands evaluated left to right whatever writing each takes: a call that changes a variable before an operand that reads it through a map read, a borrowed map, a slice or array literal, a string built in place, a closure, a struct field, a slice, a match or an if; the right side of `&&` and `||` only when the left one leaves the answer open; a channel receive, and a `mut` borrow of a map entry that makes the entry, each in its turn |
| self-handles.snello | Types holding handles on themselves: a tree with `Weak` parents and `Rc` children, an `Arc` list, a node with a `Deque` of nodes, a `Weak` on a cell whose value is gone |

A program that reads files would have them in a folder named after it with the suffix `.files`, which the test copies beside the binary.
